title: Rome Was Not Built in a Day—and Never Finished
summary: A map-history of Rome from 753 BC to today: every era builds on the last, the city's rings growing from a ploughed square (0.1 km²) to a metropolitan ring (346 km²). It is not finished.

fields.director_notes: Directed by MiniMax M3.1 Flash through SandBase (direct() calls in m31.mjs): it wrote the title, nine era narrations, event titles and all illustration prompts from a human-provided fact-checked brief (rome_brief.mjs); a second M3.1 pass revised narrations and the outro (polish_story.mjs, fix_outro.mjs). Humans edited only verified dates and areas and stripped negative phrasing from image prompts. Voice: MiniMax Speech 2.8 HD via SandBase (11 narration clips). Landmark cards: Qwen Image 3 via SandBase (2) and FLUX via Pollinations free tier (16) after the SandBase credit ran out — all card prompts are M3.1's. Map: real OpenStreetMap extents (Servian/Aurelian walls, Grande Raccordo Anulare) pulled by code (resolve.mjs, 19k+ ways) and drawn on a headless-Chrome canvas, one frame per t, encoded by FFmpeg, rendered on GitHub Actions CI. No keyframes or hand animation: every frame is a pure function of time (window.render(t)). The workflow and facts live in the open-source repo: github.com/xarkgg/rome-film-pipeline.
fields.my_city_line: New rings drawn on old ones, still moving outward.
